chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abbad ibn Sulayman from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami from his father from Ishaq ibn Ammar al-Sayrafi, who said:

I was in Kufa, and many brothers would come to me. I disliked fame, so I feared that I would become known for my religion. Therefore, I ordered my servant: whenever one of them came to me seeking me, say, 'He is not here.'
I performed Hajj that year and met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). I noticed heaviness and a change in his demeanor towards me.
I said, 'May I be your ransom, what has changed me in your eyes?' He said, 'What has changed you is [your attitude] towards the believers.'
I said, 'May I be your ransom, I only feared fame, and Allah knows the intensity of my love for them.'
He said, 'O Ishaq! Do not tire of visiting your brothers. Indeed, when a believer meets his believing brother and says
Then when they shake hands, Allah sends down between their thumbs ninety-nine mercies for the one who loves his companion more.
Then Allah turns His face towards both of them, and the one who loves his companion more receives a greater turning of Allah's face.
When they embrace, mercy overwhelms them. If they remain seated desiring only His face, not seeking any worldly goal, it is said to them: 'May Allah forgive you, so renew [your meeting].'
When they turn to conversation, the angels say to one another: 'Step aside from them, for they have a secret, and Allah has concealed it from them.'
Ishaq said: I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, will our words not be recorded? For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has said:
The son of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took a deep sigh, then wept until his tears dyed his beard.
He said, 'O Ishaq! Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, only commanded the angels to withdraw from the two believers when they meet, out of reverence for them.'
So if the angels do not record their words nor know their speech, then the Guardian over them, the Knower of the Secret and the Hidden, knows it.
'O Ishaq! Fear Allah as if you are seeing Him. If you do not see Him, then He sees you.'

'If you think that He does not see you, then you have disbelieved. And if you know that He sees you, yet you hide from the creatures by committing sins and appear before Him with them, then you have made Him among the least observant of those watching you.'

key_terms.عَالِمُ السِّرِّ وَ الْأَخْفَی: The Knower of the Secret and the Hidden (Divine Attribute)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for meeting and conversing with a fellow believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarah* (visiting) and social connectivity among believers, countering the ascetic tendency of *Khusūfah* (hiding from people) which Imam al-Sadiq (AS) viewed as a neglect of communal rights. The Imam elaborates on the metaphysical rewards of physical interaction—such as the descent of mercy during handshakes and embraces—while clarifying that the angels' silence during private conversations honors the believers' intimacy rather than implying a lack of divine recording. Ultimately, the narration serves as a reminder that hiding sins from creation while standing before God is a form of spiritual hypocrisy, urging believers to maintain *Muraqabah* (awareness of God) in both public and private spheres.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from ’Abaad b. Sulayman from Muhammad b. Sulayman al-Daylami from his father from Ishaq b. Ammar al-Sayrafi who said:

“O Ishaq! The Almighty Allah orders the angels to stay away from believers while they are conversing so that they do not note down the conversation nor do they know about it. Their conversation is known to only Allah, the Guardian of secrets.

O Ishaq! Fear Allah as if you are seeing Him because even if you cannot see Him, He is definitely looking at you. If you think that He is not seeing you, you will become an infidel. If you have a belief that He is looking you and you hide your sins from other creatures and reveal them in front of Allah you have really underestimated His Sight.”
